Ora FacePass · FP06 launch · September 2026

FP06 Creative Kit

Fourteen static concepts, each rendered at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 for Meta feed, Stories and Reels. Eleven for homeowners (the Lowe's retail lane), three for Colorado property managers. Every ad makes one claim, keeps the face as one option among several, and carries a Reserve or Walkthrough call to action.

Palette

Stone and paper for daylight concepts, dusk for night and privacy concepts. One amber accent that stands for sunlight and the unlock moment. The lock is charcoal, so every ground was picked to give it an edge.

Type

Archivo, extended

Headlines in Archivo at a wide width. Body in IBM Plex Sans. Spec labels and eyebrows in IBM Plex Mono, the way a spec sheet reads.

Layout rules

Product photography on a door slab, never floating. Headline never crosses the product. Text kept out of the top 14% and bottom 20% on 9:16. Minimum type size 22 px at 1080 wide so it survives a phone screen.

How to use the kit

  1. Upload the 4:5 file for feeds, 9:16 for Stories and Reels, 1:1 for Marketplace and right column. Meta will crop anything else.
  2. Paste the primary text, headline and description from the copy panel. Do not rewrite the headline in the image to match; the image and the text are meant to say two different things.
  3. Name every ad OFP_FP06_HO_H03_4x5_v1 style: entity, product, set (HO or PM), concept, ratio, version. The concept ID matches the file name.
  4. Hold any concept with an open verify note until Jacky confirms the fact. The notes are in amber under each concept.
  5. Rotate: launch with H01, H03, H04 and H10 in the homeowner set. Add the rest after the first 48 hours of data.

Re-render or edit

  • Source: marketing/fp06-launch/ads/src/template.html and concepts.js. Edit copy in concepts.js, then run node render.mjs.
  • Fonts and product cutouts ship with the source, so the render is reproducible on any machine with Node and Playwright.
  • Product images are Jacky's renders with the background removed. Do not replace them with AI-generated renders of the lock.
  • No em dashes anywhere in copy. Sentence case. One claim per ad.
